Apply today to build the new era of construction autonomy at Caterpillar.
We are seeking an AI Automation Engineer to develop annotation automation solutions used to create training data for robotics, autonomy, computer vision, and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) systems with a scrum team.
This role combines software engineering, machine learning, and data engineering to build automated annotation and captioning capabilities for real-world heavy equipment and construction environments. You will help deploy and extend technologies such as NVIDIA Cosmos Curator and Cosmos Reason while also developing Caterpillar-specific AI models that enable automated labeling, automated captioning, and AI-driven quality assurance.
This is a hands-on technical role focused on turning complex AI and data challenges into scalable production solutions.
What You'll Do
Develop and deploy automated labeling and captioning solutions for perception and VLA datasets.
Train, fine-tune, and evaluate AI models to support auto-labeling, auto-captioning, and annotation quality automation.
Build data pipelines and workflows that move datasets through automated labeling, human review, quality validation, and dataset publication.
Implement and extend platforms such as NVIDIA Cosmos Curator, Cosmos Reason, and other emerging AI automation technologies.
Develop solutions that integrate Caterpillar data systems with external annotation providers and human-in-the-loop workflows.
Ensure reliability, scalability, observability, and operational excellence across annotation automation services.
What Makes This Role Unique
Most AI automation solutions are not trained to understand heavy equipment, jobsites, sensor data, or machine operations.
In this role, you'll help develop the AI capabilities needed to label and describe Caterpillar-specific data at scale. You'll work on challenges involving computer vision, multimodal AI, robotics, autonomy, and Vision-Language-Action systems while helping create the data foundation that powers the future of intelligent machines.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related field.
Experience developing production-grade software solutions using Python, modern software engineering practices and containerization platforms (e.g. Docker, Kubernetes)
Experience designing and implementing distributed systems, APIs, and data processing pipelines.
Experience training, fine-tuning, or deploying machine learning models.
Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work across multiple technical disciplines.
Experience generating and managing camera and LiDAR sensor datasets for perception or machine learning applications, including data collection pipeline design and ground truth generation.
Experience in data annotation and quality assurance for autonomous systems or computer vision projects, with demonstrated ability to define annotation guidelines, identify labeling defects, and drive measurable improvements in dataset accuracy.
Experience using annotation and dataset management tools such as Labelbox, Supervisely, RoboFlow or similar toolchains.
Experience using machine learning frameworks and training tools such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, Weights & Biases, MLflow or similar frameworks.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with computer vision, robotics, autonomy, Physical AI, or multimodal AI systems.

About Beyond the Game Health
Beyond the Game Health (BTGH) is a sports-health company connecting athletes, healthcare organizations, brands and communities to turn athlete influence into measurable health engagement and outcomes.
BTGH works at the intersection of sports, healthcare, technology, community engagement and athlete-powered storytelling.
We are currently developing
BTGH OS™: The Operating System for Athlete-Powered Health Engagement
, a technology platform designed to connect athletes, health organizations, brands, events and communities through measurable engagement.
What We're Building
We are moving BTGH OS from product concept and mockups into its first functional MVP.
The first release is intentionally focused. We are not trying to build the entire vision at once.
The MVP needs to demonstrate a working journey where an athlete, event or campaign can connect a user with relevant health content, drive a measurable action, and provide partners with visibility into engagement and outcomes.
The initial product thesis is:
Athlete + Event + Health Content → User Engagement → Measurable Action → Partner Analytics
For example, someone attending a BTGH event might engage with an athlete-led health campaign, access educational content, take a specific action such as completing a screening, requesting a resource or registering for a program, and generate measurable engagement data that can be surfaced to the participating health or brand partner.
This MVP will be tested through real BTGH events and campaigns and used in demonstrations, partner conversations and fundraising as we continue building toward the broader BTGH OS vision.
What You'll Work On
We're looking for a technically strong, execution-oriented intern who can work alongside our existing team to help build and deploy the first functional version of BTGH OS.
Responsibilities may include:
Translating existing product concepts, workflows and mockups into functional product features
Developing responsive web-based user experiences for athletes, consumers/patients and partners
Building front-end and back-end functionality for the MVP
Creating athlete, event, campaign and health-content profiles
Developing user engagement and action-tracking capabilities
Building QR/link-based campaign journeys that can connect physical events and athlete content to digital experiences
Creating forms, calls-to-action and workflows that capture measurable user actions
Developing basic partner-facing dashboards showing campaign engagement and outcomes
Building and maintaining databases and APIs
Supporting authentication and role-based access as appropriate
Integrating third-party APIs and services when needed
Helping establish analytics, event tracking and data architecture
Testing, debugging and documenting the platform
Supporting deployment and ongoing MVP iterations
Working with the product team to prioritize what must be built now versus what belongs on the longer-term roadmap
Considering privacy, security and responsible data collection as health-related functionality evolves
What the First MVP Needs to Prove
Success is not measured by how many features we can build.
The first release should demonstrate that BTGH can create a measurable digital journey connecting:
Athlete + Event + Health Content → User Engagement → Measurable Action → Partner Analytics
That means we need to be able to answer questions such as:
Who engaged? What content or athlete drove the engagement? What action did the user take? Which event or campaign generated it? What can we responsibly report back to the participating partner?
The MVP should be functional enough to deploy in a real BTGH activation, collect meaningful engagement data and demonstrate the product to prospective healthcare partners, sponsors and investors.

description_preview:
Description
Do you want to shape the future of virtualized (SDN) networking in the world’s biggest public cloud?
The Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) VPC Packet Pipeline team owns the packet pipeline that runs right beneath all our customer's EC2 VPC instances, adding features like firewalling (security groups), billing and monitoring as we touch every single packet on every single host across our massive worldwide fleet. Our vision is to combine the performance of bare metal networking while maintaining all the benefits of the cloud, including delivering features not possible on bare metal i.e. true Software Defined Networking (SDN).
We are seeking an Embedded Software Development Engineer II (C/C++) to join our EC2 Nitro Fairness team, where you'll help ensure equitable resource allocation in our multi-tenant cloud infrastructure while maintaining the single-tenant experience customers expect. In this role, you'll develop sophisticated algorithms and systems that intelligently manage shared compute, memory,
and network resources across diverse customer workloads. You'll design and implement sophisticated fairness algorithms, real-time resource schedulers, and performance isolation systems that operate at microsecond latencies across millions of concurrent EC2 instances within the Nitro hypervisor. This position requires deep understanding of virtualization technologies, distributed systems, and performance optimization, as you'll be directly impacting how millions of EC2 instances share underlying hardware while appearing completely isolated to end users. You'll collaborate closely with hardware teams, hypervisor engineers, and service owners to implement fairness policies that balance resource utilization efficiency with strict performance guarantees.
Key job responsibilities
Technical Leadership & Development
Lead architecture decisions for fairness algorithms and resource allocation systems within the Nitro hypervisor
Mentor junior engineers on low-level C/Rust programming and embedded system development practices
Conduct design and code reviews for performance-critical fairness mechanisms
Drive implementation of resource isolation and scheduling policies in embedded Nitro environments
Performance Analysis & Optimization
Analyze customer workload patterns to identify fairness violations and noisy neighbor scenarios
Design and implement hardware-aware fairness algorithms leveraging CPU cache locality, memory bandwidth, and network resources
Collaborate with hardware engineering teams to optimize packet-pipeline software and hardware offloads for equitable resource sharing

Cross-Team Collaboration & Strategy
Partner with hardware/firmware teams on co-designing fairness enforcements
Collaborate with other engineering vertical teams to ensure fairness features integrate seamlessly across the stack
Communicate fairness requirements and technical designs to senior management and product teams
Evaluate emerging technologies for ML-based instance types and their impact on resource fairness
System Design & Implementation
Develop real-time fairness monitoring and enforcement systems operating at microsecond latencies
Implement dynamic resource allocation policies that adapt to changing workload characteristics
Design telemetry and observability systems to measure and validate fairness across multi-tenant environments

description_preview:
Responsibilities
Team Introduction
Global E-Commerce (TikTok Shop) is one of TikTok's fastest-growing businesses and a core driver of the company's revenue growth. Our team, Global E-Commerce Content Recommendation, owns the end-to-end recommendation stack for e-commerce video and image-text content on TikTok worldwide — retrieval, ranking, and multi-queue blending; supply ecosystem and cold start; and the browsing-to-purchase experience for hundreds of millions of users.
We are building what we intend to be the most advanced recommendation system in the world, on top of a two-sided marketplace that is still growing fast. Many of the problems that matter most here — what to optimize, how to know it worked, how to treat a brand-new seller fairly — have no settled answer anywhere in the industry.
We are looking for talented individuals to join our team. As a graduate, you will get opportunities to pursue bold ideas, tackle complex challenges, and unlock limitless growth.
Successful candidates must be able to commit to an onboarding date by the end of the year. Please state your availability and graduation date clearly in your resume.
Candidates can apply to a maximum of two positions and will be considered for jobs in the order you apply. The application limit is applicable to our Company and its affiliates' jobs globally. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis - we encourage you to apply early.
Responsibilities:
Optimize the recommendation models across the full funnel: You own the models behind TikTok Shop's product, short-video, and livestream recommendation — retrieval, pre-ranking, ranking, re-ranking, and multi-queue blending — and every iteration ships to real traffic. Core threads:
Ranking and retrieval models. Iterate the model architectures that carry the funnel: multi-task and multi-objective learning from click through conversion and GMV; multi-scenario, multi-format joint modelling; and the sample, label, and debiasing design that decides what the model actually learns.
User interest modelling. Ultra-long behavior sequences (10K+ events) with real trade-offs between positional-encoding extrapolation, attention cost, and online latency and storage; decoupling stable preferences from seasonal demand, momentary impulses, and needs already satisfied; and mining implicit negative feedback — impressions without clicks, consecutive skips, fast swipes — at every stage of the funnel.
Multimodal representation learning. Combine product images, text, and video content with behavioural data into high-quality item and user representations.
Re-ranking, blending, and exploration. List-level decisions rather than pointwise scores: multi-queue blending across content types, diversity and repetition control, and exploration mechanisms that surface interests users have not yet expressed — while breaking the recommendation feedback loop.
Design the cold-start and content-ecosystem mechanisms: New products, new livestream hosts, and new creators arrive in volume every day.
Do original work on open problems. Long-term value modelling, repurchase and retention, transaction attribution, fatigue modelling, new-user recommendation, incremental value modelling, LLM4Rec — the frontier problems of a real recommendation system, where the industry has no standard answers.

Fluent in a deep-learning framework (PyTorch / TensorFlow) and at least one large-scale data-processing tool (Spark / Flink / SQL); proficient in Python, with working C++ and Linux skills.

Description
Amazon's Intermodal (AZIM) Network Optimization team is looking for a Business Intelligence Engineer to build the data foundation and analytical tooling that powers cost optimization across the intermodal network. This is a hands-on role responsible for transforming complex, high-volume supply chain data into automated pipelines, self-service dashboards, and deep-dive analyses that surface cost reduction opportunities and drive operational decisions.
Working closely with product managers, supply chain managers, and business stakeholders, you'll own the end-to-end analytics lifecycle — from data modeling and ETL development to visualization and insight generation. The ideal candidate combines strong technical skills in SQL, data engineering, and statistical analysis with genuine curiosity about the business, and thrives in a fast-paced environment where the quality and speed of your analytics directly shape where the network invests to reduce cost and improve efficiency.
Key job responsibilities
Data Pipeline & Infrastructure Design, build, and maintain scalable ETL pipelines and data models that consolidate intermodal cost, volume, and operational data into reliable, query-ready datasets.
Dashboards & Self-Service Analytics Develop and maintain automated dashboards and reporting mechanisms that give stakeholders real-time visibility into cost drivers, network performance, and optimization opportunities — reducing manual reporting effort.
Deep-Dive Analysis Conduct rigorous analyses on cost trends, operational inefficiencies, and network anomalies to identify root causes and quantify savings opportunities. Translate raw data into clear, actionable recommendations.
Metrics & Data Quality Define, instrument, and monitor key business metrics. Establish data quality checks and validation frameworks to ensure analytics are accurate and trusted across the org.
Automation & Tooling Identify manual, repetitive analytical workflows and automate them — building reusable tools and queries that scale the team's analytical capacity.
Cross-Functional Partnership Partner with Product, Supply Chain Managers, Finance, and Operations to understand analytical needs, prioritize requests, and deliver data solutions that inform cost optimization decisions.
A day in the life
You'll start each morning validating overnight data pipeline runs and checking dashboards for anomalies or data quality issues. From there, you'll dig into an analytical deep dive — querying large datasets to size a cost savings opportunity, investigating a network anomaly, or building a new metric requested by the team. You'll partner with Product Managers and Supply Chain Managers to translate business questions into data solutions, and collaborate with Finance to align on cost baselines and definitions. You'll spend time building — writing ETL code, refining data models, or automating a manual report. When you uncover an insight, you'll package it into a clear visualization or write-up for stakeholders and leadership.

At Bot Auto, we build autonomous trucks to transform the way goods are transported and improve the quality of life for communities worldwide. We are seeking a VCU Software Engineer to design, implement, integrate, and validate production-grade embedded software for advanced vehicle control systems. This role owns work across requirements, architecture, model-based development, embedded C/C++, AUTOSAR integration, and MIL/SIL/HIL validation. Software System Design
Own the VCU software lifecycle from requirements analysis and architecture through implementation, integration, validation, release, and field support.

Translate vehicle-level requirements into clear, testable software requirements with end-to-end traceability.
Partner with controls, hardware, systems, autonomy, validation, manufacturing, and service teams to optimize performance, safety, reliability, and diagnosability.

Verification & Validation
Define and execute unit, integration, MIL, SIL, and HIL test strategies, including requirement-based tests, fault injection, and regression coverage.
Automate build, test, and reporting workflows within CI/CD pipelines, and use results to drive measurable quality improvements.
Support bench and vehicle integration, diagnose cross-domain hardware/software issues, reproduce failures from logs, and drive issues to verified closure.

Contribute to design reviews, coding and modeling standards, knowledge sharing, and mentorship while continuously improving the team's development practices.

Demonstrated experience developing and delivering embedded software for automotive, robotics, autonomous systems, or other safety-critical real-time products.
Strong embedded C/C++ skills and practical knowledge of real-time systems, microcontrollers, memory constraints, concurrency, and hardware/software interfaces.
Hands-on proficiency with MATLAB, Simulink, and Stateflow for model-based design, simulation, and production software development.
Solid understanding of vehicle control concepts, feedback control, state machines, fault detection, degraded modes, and safety mechanisms.
Experience with in-vehicle networks and diagnostics, including CAN/CAN-FD and working knowledge of UDS, XCP, or equivalent protocols.
Working knowledge of AUTOSAR Classic architecture and the interaction among application software, RTE, BSW, and MCAL.
Experience with requirement-based development and MIL, SIL, HIL, bench, or vehicle-level verification.
Proficiency with version control, code review, issue tracking, automated testing, CI/CD, and structured debugging workflows.
Strong analytical, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills, with ownership from ambiguous problem definition through validated delivery.

Practical exposure to ISO 26262, Automotive SPICE, MISRA C/C++, safety analysis, or safety-oriented development processes.
Experience with Vector, dSPACE, ETAS, or similar tools for network analysis, measurement, calibration, rapid prototyping, and HIL testing.
Hands-on experience with CANoe/CANalyzer, DaVinci Configurator/Developer, Embedded Coder, TargetLink, or comparable toolchains.
Python experience for test automation, log processing, data analysis, reporting, or developer tooling.
Experience with ECU bring-up, board-level debugging, vehicle testing, drive-by-wire systems, or autonomous/electric vehicle platforms.

description_preview:
We’re reinventing the market research industry. Let’s reinvent it together.
At Numerator, we believe tomorrow’s success starts with today’s market intelligence. We empower the world’s leading brands and retailers with unmatched insights into consumer behavior and the influencers that drive it.
Numerator’s Data Science team provides statistical and methodological leadership across the organization, developing the methodologies, tools, and data products that support our products.
This is a wide-ranging applied data science role focused primarily on the consumer purchase panel underlying our largest products, with opportunities to contribute to other complex data science initiatives across Numerator’s broader product portfolio. The work combines applied statistics, data investigation, methodology development, and practical implementation. Many of the questions we tackle do not have a single observable right answer, requiring us to combine statistical evidence, product context, and subject-matter judgment to understand tradeoffs and determine whether a solution improves the product as a whole. As your expertise grows, you will take on increasingly complex work and have opportunities to deepen your technical expertise, lead projects, improve team practices, and shape how we work.
How You’ll Spend Your Time
Design and implement statistical methodologies that improve the representativeness, stability, and quality of Numerator’s products.
Develop data science solutions to problems involving consumer behavior, panel composition, and data quality using techniques such as sampling, weighting, statistical modeling, classification, predictive modeling, anomaly detection, and optimization.
Build scalable Python and SQL solutions, internal tools, and data products that turn statistical methodologies into reliable production workflows.
Develop metrics, monitoring, and validation frameworks to evaluate system performance and identify unexpected or unintended behavior.
Contribute throughout the project lifecycle, from problem definition and exploration through implementation, testing, deployment, and ongoing evaluation.
Work closely with Product, Engineering, Data Operations, and business partners to shape requirements and develop solutions that are both statistically sound and practical to use.
Communicate methodologies, findings, assumptions, and tradeoffs clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
What You'll Bring to Numerator
A bachelor’s or advanced degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Data Science, Computer Science, Economics, Physics, or another quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.
Two to five years of industry experience developing and delivering data science solutions.
A strong foundation in applied statistics, with experience applying statistical modeling, optimization, or other quantitative methods to real-world data problems.
Proficiency in Python and SQL, including experience developing reusable, well-structured code and working with large, complex datasets.
Comfort working through open-ended problems, investigating unexpected results, and developing solutions with guidance and collaboration, along with the ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical partners.
Familiarity with survey research or consumer panels—including sampling, weighting, bias correction, imputation, or other methods used to improve representativeness—is helpful but not required.
Experience working with user-level or behavioral data is helpful, as is exposure to production data science workflows and tools such as Snowflake, AWS, Airflow, or GitHub.
Familiarity with AI-powered tools and workflows, with an interest in applying emerging technologies to improve productivity, learning, and outcomes.
What We Offer
An inclusive and collaborative company culture—we work in an open environment while working together to get things done and adapt to changing needs as they arise.
A market-competitive total compensation package.
Volunteer time off and charitable donation matching.
Strong support for career growth, including mentorship programs, leadership training, access to conferences, and employee resource groups.
A great benefits package including health, vision, and dental coverage; a Personal Spending Account; unlimited PTO; flexible scheduling; 401(k) matching; travel reimbursement; and more.

We run one of the largest digital marketplaces in residential real estate, where buyers, sellers, servicers, and agents transact on real property with real money at stake. Every listing that moves through our platform touches valuation, bidding, contracts, payments, and a long list of external systems, and the platform keeps evolving to meet the needs of the market.
We’re hiring full stack engineers to build that platform. You’ll work in React and TypeScript on the front end, Node, Kotlin, and GraphQL services behind it, running on AWS and Kubernetes. You’ll own features end to end: design, build, test, ship, and support them in production.
What The Work Looks Like
You’ll work in a lean technology org (~50 engineers) which means there is no layer between you and the work that matters. What you build ships.
You’ll ship customer-facing features and the services that power them, usually in slices small enough to get in front of users quickly.
You’ll test what you build. That means automated coverage at the unit, integration, API, and end-to-end levels, wired into CI so it keeps working after you move on. We don’t hand code to someone else to verify.
You’ll debug real problems in production. Distributed systems fail in interesting ways, and figuring out why is part of the job, not an interruption to it.
You’ll be in design discussions and code reviews as a participant, not an observer. If you think an approach is wrong, we want to hear it early.
You’ll work directly with product, UX, data, and other engineers. Most of the interesting decisions happen in those conversations.
You’ll have room to build AI-enabled features. We’re actively putting LLMs into customer and internal workflows, and engineers here are shaping what that looks like.
Who Does Well Here
The technical bar matters, but these are the traits that actually predict who thrives on this team.
You get curious when something doesn’t add up.
A weird log line, a metric that moved for no reason, a function nobody can explain. You go find out why instead of routing around it.
Blockers are problems, not stop signs.
Everyone gets stuck. What matters is what you do in the next hour. You try a few angles, read the source, check the logs, and when you do ask for help you show up with what you’ve already ruled out.
You’re still learning.
You picked up something new in the last few months, probably because you wanted to rather than because someone assigned it. You can also say “I don’t know” without it costing you anything.
You care whether it worked.
Not whether the ticket closed, whether the customer’s problem is actually solved.
What You Bring
Roughly 3+ years building and shipping production software
React, or another modern component framework you can translate from
Node.js or Kotlin/Java backend services, with REST or GraphQL APIs
Hands-on experience in AWS or a comparable cloud
Enough comfort with Docker and Kubernetes that a container deployment isn’t a black box
Automated testing as a habit rather than a phase
Working knowledge of CI/CD, plus relational and NoSQL data stores
Judgment about performance, scalability, and security, and the instinct to ask about them before shipping
If you have most of this and a track record of picking up the rest quickly, apply anyway. We’d rather hire someone who learns fast than someone who checked every box five years ago.
AI and emerging technology
You don’t need to be an AI or ML engineer. We’re looking for software engineers who are genuinely curious about this space and want to apply it to real customer problems.
Any of the following is a plus: LLM and generative AI application work, AI API integrations, AWS Bedrock or comparable platforms, retrieval-augmented generation, conversational interfaces, or agent and workflow automation. Personal projects count.
Nice to have
Background in fintech, proptech, real estate, mortgage, lending, payments, e-commerce, or marketplaces
Experience with high-volume transactional systems
Microservices, distributed systems, or event-driven architecture
Experience on a team where engineers owned both delivery and quality
How We Engineer
Quality is part of engineering, not a separate department. Engineers here test what they build and own it through production.
We keep feedback loops short. Trunk-based development, feature flags, small changes, frequent deploys.
We prefer clarity over cleverness, in code and in conversation.
We hire people who are curious, direct, and accountable, and then give them problems worth solving.

title: Security Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering
reason: Stack +36; Title fit +6; Exp fit +10; US +10; Senior desc -15
description_preview:
Description
AWS Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) embeds AI engineers directly inside strategic enterprise customers to design, build, and deploy production-grade AI systems. We are looking for a Security Engineer to join the FDE security team and help secure production AI systems deployed in customer environments.
You will conduct security reviews, write security tooling, perform threat modeling, and implement controls that protect AI systems built by FDE engineers. You work alongside FDE delivery pods in customer environments, getting hands-on with production code, cloud infrastructure, and AI/ML pipelines. You learn fast, ship fast, and build security into the system rather than bolting it on after the fact.
This is a hands-on security engineering role where you spend most of your time writing code, reviewing architectures, and testing systems. You work with senior security engineers who will mentor you, but you own real security deliverables from your first engagement. If you want to learn AI security by doing it, in production, at enterprise scale, this is the role.
This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen.
Key job responsibilities
Conduct security design reviews, code reviews, and architecture assessments for production AI systems (agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, orchestration layers, model integrations) under guidance from senior security engineers
Perform threat modeling and penetration testing for AI/ML applications deployed in customer environments; identify vulnerabilities and work with FDE engineers to implement fixes before production release
Build and maintain security automation: scanning tools, CI/CD security gates, guardrail testing scripts, secrets detection, and dependency vulnerability checks for forward-deployed AI systems
Implement security controls for AI-specific threats: prompt injection prevention, output filtering, data isolation, model API endpoint hardening, and guardrail configuration
Support security incident response for FDE-delivered production AI systems; assist with triage, root cause analysis, and remediation under senior engineer guidance
Document security findings, patterns, and remediation guidance as reusable playbooks and runbooks that benefit future FDE engagements
Contribute to the FDE security accelerator library: reusable modules, templates, and reference configurations that help FDE engineers build secure AI systems faster
Requires up to 25% travel
A day in the life
You start the morning running your automated security scan against a new Bedrock-powered application an FDE pod shipped overnight, triaging the findings and filing issues for two real vulnerabilities. Mid-morning you pair with an FDE engineer to fix an IAM policy that's overly permissive for their multi-agent orchestration system. After lunch you're writing a Python script that automates guardrail bypass testing for the team's standard deployment pattern. You close out the day joining a threat modeling session led by a senior security engineer, where you learn how to assess data flow risks in a customer's RAG pipeline. Every week you're working on a different AI architecture, building skills you can't get anywhere else.

AWS Forward Deployed Engineering embeds AI engineers directly inside strategic enterprise customers to build production AI systems. AWS invested $1B in this initiative. Description
AWS Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) embeds AI engineers directly inside strategic enterprise customers to design, build, and deploy production-grade AI systems. We are looking for a Security Engineer to join the FDE security team and help secure production AI systems deployed in customer environments.
You will conduct security reviews, write security tooling, perform threat modeling, and implement controls that protect AI systems built by FDE engineers. You work alongside FDE delivery pods in customer environments, getting hands-on with production code, cloud infrastructure, and AI/ML pipelines. You learn fast, ship fast, and build security into the system rather than bolting it on after the fact.
This is a hands-on security engineering role where you spend most of your time writing code, reviewing architectures, and testing systems. You work with senior security engineers who will mentor you, but you own real security deliverables from your first engagement. If you want to learn AI security by doing it, in production, at enterprise scale, this is the role.
This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen.
Key job responsibilities
Conduct security design reviews, code reviews, and architecture assessments for production AI systems (agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, orchestration layers, model integrations) under guidance from senior security engineers
Perform threat modeling and penetration testing for AI/ML applications deployed in customer environments; identify vulnerabilities and work with FDE engineers to implement fixes before production release
Build and maintain security automation: scanning tools, CI/CD security gates, guardrail testing scripts, secrets detection, and dependency vulnerability checks for forward-deployed AI systems
Implement security controls for AI-specific threats: prompt injection prevention, output filtering, data isolation, model API endpoint hardening, and guardrail configuration
Support security incident response for FDE-delivered production AI systems; assist with triage, root cause analysis, and remediation under senior engineer guidance
Document security findings, patterns, and remediation guidance as reusable playbooks and runbooks that benefit future FDE engagements
Contribute to the FDE security accelerator library: reusable modules, templates, and reference configurations that help FDE engineers build secure AI systems faster
Requires up to 25% travel

You start the morning running your automated security scan against a new Bedrock-powered application an FDE pod shipped overnight, triaging the findings and filing issues for two real vulnerabilities. After lunch you're writing a Python script that automates guardrail bypass testing for the team's standard deployment pattern. You close out the day joining a threat modeling session led by a senior security engineer, where you learn how to assess data flow risks in a customer's RAG pipeline. Every week you're working on a different AI architecture, building skills you can't get anywhere else.

Life at Intel

As a Strategic/Development Industrial Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in designing and implementing solutions that drive Intel's manufacturing efficiency and long-term capacity planning capabilities. Your work will directly contribute to Intel's ability to innovate and meet the demands of a dynamic global market.
Business group
You will join Intel Foundry's Factory Capacity Optimization (FCO) organization, a team responsible for factory space, capacity, and capital planning. This group leads Intel's growth strategy by enabling data-driven decisions that align with long-term manufacturing objectives. As part of the FCO Network Design team, you'll collaborate across manufacturing operations, technology development, and finance to support Intel's mission of delivering cutting-edge technologies with scalability and efficiency.
Key Responsibilities
Develop and execute space, capacity, and capital strategies for APTM WPM (Advanced Packaging Technology Manufacturing - Wafer Packaging Manufacturing) factories to balancing near term execution and long range planning through scenario-based tradeoff analysis.
Model WPM (Wafer Packaging Manufacturing) capacity across specific manufacturing segments, incorporating demand forecasts, tool roadmaps, and customer scenarios and demand-capacity tradeoffs to inform factory response options.
Perform SnOP demand and capacity analysis evaluating gaps, constraints, and responses scenarios including one or more APTM manufacturing segments and translate insights into clear executive-ready recommendations on capacity actions, capital timing, and tradeoffs.
Analyze tradeoffs between space, capacity, throughput, and CapEx to optimize factory economics and return on invested capital (ROIC), framing implications for decision timing and risk.
Integrate capacity strategies across APTM organizations, Technology Development (TD), Manufacturing, Foundry Business Group (FBG), Foundry Construction and Sourcing, Foundry Customer Strategic Planning, and Finance to ensure alignment and executable decision timing.
Collect, benchmark, and synthesize internal and external data to develop structured insights and recommendations for senior and executive leadership.
Own and develop new planning or modeling capability within the organization, driving rapid maturity, adoption, and sustained impact.
Communicate clearly under tight timelines and incomplete information, making sound assumptions when data is unavailable and upleveling insights to influence outcomes across a diverse cross-functional stakeholder set.

1+ years' experience with project management; experience managing multiple priorities in fast-paced manufacturing environments.

Job Title: Embedded Software Engineer
Job Description
We are seeking a highly skilled Embedded Software Engineer to design, develop, and integrate software for embedded systems. This role covers the full development lifecycle from requirements analysis and design to implementation, testing, and validation with a focus on delivering robust and reliable solutions. The role includes a strong emphasis on testing and validation to ensure functionality and reliability. In addition to technical development, the ideal candidate will contribute to proposal efforts by translating requirements into actionable work tasks and providing accurate effort estimates. Strong communication skills and the ability to present and explain software solutions to internal teams and customers are essential.
Responsibilities
Perform full lifecycle development for embedded systems, including implementation, unit testing, integration, and formal sell-off testing.
Review customer requirements, translate them into specifications, and produce technical documentation, designs, operational concepts, and estimate effort.
Collaborate closely with hardware engineers to ensure seamless integration of software with electronic components and boards.
Develop and execute test plans and procedures; perform debugging, troubleshooting, and ensure compliance with functional specifications.
Conduct design and code reviews, resolve defects, and adhere to established development processes, configuration management, and release practices.
Develop and execute test plans, procedures, and automated test scripts for embedded software systems.
Review and interpret system and software requirements, ensuring traceability and compliance.
Design, develop, maintain, and debug embedded software applications using C and Python.
Perform integration, verification, and validation testing on embedded hardware and software components.
Participate in software architecture discussions, code reviews, and design evaluations.
Develop new features, enhance existing functionality, and troubleshoot software issues throughout the product lifecycle.
Utilize instrument control (single-board computers, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, power supplies) for hardware and software validation.
Collaborate closely with software and hardware engineers to troubleshoot and resolve defects, performance issues, and integration challenges.
Maintain test and development documentation, including test cases, software design records, results, and compliance reports.
Support continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines for automated build, testing, and release processes.
Conduct formal verification activities and provide evidence of requirement compliance.
Present development progress, test results, and technical findings to internal teams and customers.
Support root cause analysis of field issues and implement corrective software solutions.
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives focused on software quality, reliability, maintainability, and performance.
Essential Skills
Experience with both development and testing.
Hands-on experience with C and Python.
Experience with requirements analysis, traceability, and verification.
Familiarity with embedded hardware concepts, microcontrollers, and real-time systems.
Ability to design and maintain automated test environments.
Additional Skills & Qualifications
Experience with CI/CD tools and version control (Git).
Familiarity with communication protocols (UART, I²C, SPI, Serial RapidIO, Ethernet).
Familiarity with unit testing tools.
Familiarity with Linux environments and shell scripting.
Familiarity with MIL-STD Qualification testing.
Familiarity with manufacturing processes and Electronic Stress Screening.
Understanding of 'Bare metal' programming.
Work Environment
The work environment is primarily onsite with some flexibility. The office is cubicle-based with labs available for testing and development. The work schedule follows a 9/80 format, offering longer weekends every other week. The team has a mix of social dynamics, with some enjoying social activities like happy hours and others focusing more on family.
Job Type & Location
This is a Permanent position based out of Greenville, SC.
Pay And Benefits
The pay range for this position is $40.00 - $60.00/hr.
Individual compensation offered for this position within this range will depend on many factors, including qualifications, skills, relevant experience, job knowledge, geographic location, internal equity, and other pertinent job-related factors.
Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits and may depend on your job classification and length of employment. Benefits are subject to change and may be subject to specific elections, plan, or program terms. If eligible, the benefits available for this temporary role may include the following:
Medical, dental & vision
Critical Illness, Accident, and Hospital

Life Insurance (Voluntary Life & AD&D for the employee and dependents)
Short and long-term disability
Health Spending Account (HSA)
Transportation benefits
Employee Assistance Program

Job Details
Job Description:
Why Intel Foundry
At Intel Foundry, you will help develop and qualify next-generation silicon photonics technologies that enable AI, cloud infrastructure, high-performance computing, and advanced networking solutions. Working alongside world-class scientists and engineers, you will gain hands-on experience with cutting-edge photonic devices while contributing to innovative technologies that power the future of data communications.
This role offers the opportunity to develop expertise in reliability engineering, device characterization, qualification methodologies, and semiconductor technology development within one of the industry's leading Silicon Photonics organizations.
About The Role
Intel's Silicon Photonics Quality & Reliability team is seeking a
Silicon Photonics Quality & Reliability Engineer
to support reliability assessments, qualification activities, and technology development for advanced photonic devices and photonic integrated circuits (PICs).
In this role, you will work closely with process integration, technology development, design, manufacturing, and quality teams to evaluate device reliability, analyze data, investigate failures, and support the development of robust qualification methodologies. This position provides an excellent opportunity for engineers who are passionate about photonics, semiconductor technology, reliability engineering, and continuous learning.
What You’ll Do
Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:
Support reliability characterization and qualification activities for silicon photonic devices and technologies.
Analyze reliability, characterization, and manufacturing data to identify trends, opportunities, and potential risks.
Execute Design of Experiments (DOE) and statistical analyses to evaluate device performance and reliability.
Partner with cross-functional teams to support technology development and process certification activities.
Assist with root cause investigations and failure analysis efforts using structured problem-solving methodologies.
Develop technical reports and communicate findings to engineering teams.
Support qualification testing activities including environmental, electrical, and reliability stress testing.
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance product quality, reliability, and manufacturing maturity.
Utilize data analysis tools to drive engineering decisions and improve process understanding.
Support the transfer of new technologies into manufacturing environments.
The Ideal Candidate Should Exhibit The Following Behavioral Traits
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Curiosity and enthusiasm for learning new technologies and engineering methodologies.
Ability to work effectively in a highly collaborative and cross-functional environment.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Attention to detail and a commitment to technical excellence.
Effective prioritization and organizational skills.
A proactive approach to identifying issues and driving solutions.
Ability to work in a fast-paced and evolving development environment.
Strong teamwork and interpersonal skills.
Passion for quality, reliability, and innovation.
Intel invests in our people and offers a complete and competitive package of benefits employees and their families through every stage of life.

Master's degree in Optical Science, Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Semiconductor Engineering, or a related technical field with 1+ years of relevant experience. Or PhD in the same field with 6+ months of relevant experience.
You must have the experience described above in the following:
Silicon Photonics TD / Manufacturing experience.
Data extraction and analysis skills (JMP/ILM/REL/PCS/SQL Scripting).
QnR/Process/device/product engineering experience.

Design of Experiments (DOE) principles and structured problem solving.

Exposure to the methodology of qualifying optical devices, test methods to evaluate the device's performance and reliability (HTOL, THB/DH, MSV, TC, HTS, ESD etc.), and failure analysis.

The
Opportunity
You'll own the systems that feed Nascent's trading and research operations with the data they need to compete — building and operating the web scraping and data acquisition infrastructure that runs 24/7 across a heterogeneous fleet of machines, providers, and operating systems. This is a roughly 50/50 split between software engineering and operations: half your time you're writing production code (primarily Rust) to build new scrapers, defeat anti-bot countermeasures, and architect resilient pipelines; the other half you're deep in logs, monitoring dashboards, and fleet health — diagnosing failures, tuning proxies, and keeping a distributed system humming across mixed infrastructure.
You'll work closely with analysts and researchers who depend on the data you deliver. The problems are genuinely interesting: every major website is actively trying to stop you, infrastructure spans multiple cloud providers and bare metal, and the surface area of what breaks is enormous. This role is remote-first. Montreal proximity is preferred — the team has a growing analyst presence there and in-person collaboration matters — but it's not a hard requirement. North American or European time zones work best for team overlap.
Responsibilities
Build and maintain production-grade web scraping systems — primarily in Rust — designing scrapers that are resilient to site changes, rate limiting, CAPTCHAs, and evolving anti-bot countermeasures.
Operate and monitor a heterogeneous distributed infrastructure spanning multiple cloud providers, bare metal, and mixed operating systems — you own uptime, not just deployments.
Diagnose production issues from raw logs and telemetry, building observability into every system you ship so problems surface before they cascade.
Design and implement proxy management, rotation strategies, and network-layer evasion techniques to maintain reliable data acquisition at scale.
Develop tooling for fleet health monitoring, automated alerting, and self-healing infrastructure across a diverse set of machines and hosting environments.
Collaborate with analysts and researchers to understand data requirements, prioritize new source integrations, and ensure data quality and freshness meet trading-grade standards.
Reverse-engineer web applications and APIs — inspecting network traffic, deobfuscating JavaScript, and adapting to adversarial changes in target sites.
Continuously improve system reliability, throughput, and maintainability — refactoring scraping pipelines, optimizing connection handling, and reducing operational toil through automation.
Deploy and maintain agentic workflows for data source discovery, onboarding, and troubleshooting — using LLM-based agents to automate the identification of new sources, accelerate integration, and surface and resolve failures in existing pipelines.
About You
You are a builder who also runs what you build — you don't consider a project done when the PR merges; you consider it done when it's been stable in production for weeks.
You have a genuine interest in the cat-and-mouse game of web scraping at scale: anti-bot systems, browser fingerprinting, proxy rotation, and the constant adaptation it requires.
You are comfortable navigating messy, heterogeneous infrastructure — mixed OS environments, multiple hosting providers, hardware you didn't provision — and you make it better over time.
You are energized by operational puzzles: tracing a failure across distributed logs, identifying a subtle network degradation, or figuring out why a scraper that worked yesterday is now blocked.
You write clean, production-grade code and care about systems that run unattended and fail gracefully. You are proficient in at least one major programming language (Go, Python, C++, Java, or similar) — the stack is primarily Rust, and prior Rust experience is a strong plus, but if you haven't written it professionally, you're the kind of engineer who picks up new languages fast and takes ownership of the ramp. Python is useful for scripting, prototyping, and analyst-facing tooling.
You thrive in less-structured environments where you're trusted to prioritize your own work, and you take ownership of outcomes rather than waiting for tickets.
You are fluent with agentic workflows and LLM-based tooling — you know how to design and operate AI agents to discover new data sources, automate onboarding, and triage failures in production pipelines. You don't treat AI as a novelty; you reach for it when it's the right tool and build on top of it.

At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.
Where AI Meets Medicine: Build the Future of Drug Discovery in the Heart of Silicon Valley!
Making medicine that’s never been made means doing what’s never been done. If you’re an engineer, scientist, or builder who thrives on problems no one has solved before, this is your invitation; we want you on the team. We are ready to challenge the status quo and push medicine forward, all in the name of health. Are you up for the challenge? If so, join us!
About The Lilly And NVIDIA Partnership
Lilly and NVIDIA are launching a new AI co-innovation lab in the heart of Silicon Valley — an up-to-$1 billion, multi-year commitment to solve drug discovery’s toughest challenges. The lab brings Lilly scientists, technologists, chemists and biologists together with NVIDIA engineers under one roof. Together, we are building purpose-built foundation and frontier AI models trained on Lilly data at scale, tightening the feedback loop between automated wet labs and computational dry labs, designing the next generation of medicines for millions of patients across the globe.
What You’ll Be Doing
As an ML Ops Engineer, you build and operate the platforms that run the end-to-end machine learning lifecycle. You enable reliable model deployment, operation, monitoring, retraining, and reproducibility at scale. You optimize infrastructure and GPU resources to support research and discovery workloads. You will work closely with engineering and scientific teams to deliver production-ready AI capabilities.
How You’ll Succeed
Lead the operational lifecycle of ML models, including deployment, monitoring, and ongoing reliability.
Operate and optimize large-scale inference platforms that support scientific discovery and AI workloads.
Ensure models can be deployed, scaled, monitored, and maintained in production environments.
Test, refine, and improve model accuracy.
Work with data scientists, business analysts and partners to integrate ML models into broader strategies.
Automate the platform with infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD, and document it well enough that someone else can operate it.
What You Should Bring
Strong Python skills and experience working with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow.
Experience deploying, operating, and scaling production machine learning platforms, including model serving, monitoring, and large-scale inference workloads.
Experience with MLOps platforms and tools like MLflow, Weights & Biases, KServe, or similar technologies.
Proficiency with containerization, orchestration, and distributed compute environments (Docker, Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray).
Experience operating large-scale AI platforms that deploy, host, and optimize machine learning models for production use, using technologies such as Triton, vLLM, or TensorRT-LLM.
Experience with infrastructure automation and CI/CD practices using tools such as Terraform, Ansible, GitHub Actions, or related.
Experience supporting cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and on-premises GPU infrastructure.
Knowledge of observability and operational monitoring, including metrics, logging, tracing, and performance tuning.
Ability to identify and address system, infrastructure, and model performance issues through automation and continuous improvement.
Ability to collaborate effectively with research scientists, AI engineers, and infrastructure teams in a fast-paced environment.
Your Basic Qualifications
Bachelor’s in Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related technical field
4+ years of experience in machine learning engineering, ML Ops, or platform engineering.

This role is based at our Silicon Valley Hub. We offer a flexible hybrid work model, with
three days onsite and two days working remotely each week

See it Differently - Early Careers at Arup
See it differently
You see the world through a unique lens and that’s exactly what we need. We embrace how you see things differently – it’s essential for creating a sustainable future.
Arup is a global consultancy with advisory and technical expertise across more than 150 disciplines. We guide, plan and design the future of the built environment. Globally, each year we recruit hundreds of graduates and students who help us see things differently and solve the most complex challenges facing our clients, climate and communities.
Our Controls team designs the systems that allow complex buildings and infrastructure to operate safely, efficiently, and reliably. We work across the full project lifecycle, collaborating with mechanical, electrical, plumbing, technology, and operations teams to define how equipment is monitored, controlled, integrated, and tested. Our work includes building management systems, direct digital controls, programmable logic controllers, instrumentation, system integration, communication networks, and control sequences. The team supports a broad range of technically challenging projects, transforming operational requirements and engineering concepts into coordinated designs that can be implemented, commissioned, and successfully operated.
The opportunity
Support the design of integrated control systems by developing control diagrams, points lists, network architectures, equipment schedules, instrumentation requirements, and installation details under the guidance of experienced engineers.
Develop sequences of operation and control narratives that translate mechanical and electrical system intent into clear, testable requirements for equipment staging, safeties, alarms, operating modes, and system response.

Participate throughout design and construction by assisting with technical specifications, bid evaluations, submittal and shop-drawing reviews, responses to contractor questions, field observations, and resolution of installation or integration issues.

description_preview:
We believe a story can change what a person can see: not by arguing, but by showing them something true they didn’t have words for. Dream Three is a story studio built to deliver best-in-class, genre-spanning narratives across mediums, including film and series, theater and live events, publishing and music, and digital and immersive. If you’re looking for a team that takes big creative swings and doesn’t settle for less than excellent, keep reading.
Role Overview
We’re hiring a freelance Website Developer to build, maintain, and improve websites for brands. You’ll translate approved designs and creative direction into responsive, maintainable sites; structure content so it is easy to update; and carry work through testing, launch, and handoff. This is a hands-on implementation role that combines keen visual attention to detail with sound technical judgment and dependable delivery.
What Success Looks Like
Approved pages and features launch on time, with the design preserved across agreed devices and browsers.
Forms, content, integrations, and key user journeys are tested; technical issues are prioritized and communicated clearly.
Stakeholders know what is ready, blocked, or awaiting a decision without having to repeatedly chase updates.
Sites are structured so routine content updates can be made efficiently without unnecessary developer support. Another developer can understand the implementation and its limitations.
Who You Are
A meticulous, practical builder who cares about the finished interface as much as the implementation behind it.
You take ownership of your work through launch, testing thoroughly and resolving issues rather than assuming someone else will catch them.
You scope and estimate work realistically, manage agreed milestones, and flag tradeoffs before a deadline is at risk.
You work well from creative direction, ask useful questions, and solve implementation problems without unnecessarily redesigning the brief.
Key Responsibilities
Build + Content Management: Implement responsive pages, reusable components, content-management structures, and scoped interactions from approved designs and content.
Quality + Support: Test functionality, agreed accessibility requirements, and performance; investigate defects; maintain assigned sites within agreed support coverage.
Delivery + Handoff: Recommend implementation approaches; define milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria; coordinate reviews and approved launches or migrations; and document content editing, integrations, and handoff steps.
Role Requirements
3+ years of relevant website-development experience, or equivalent demonstrated work. Show sites you personally implemented and explain your contribution.
Strong hands-on ability in Webflow or Wix Studio, plus HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The approved approach is determined per assignment.
Experience with CMS architecture, responsive design, practical testing, and clear communication across website builds and ongoing improvements.
BONUS POINTS
Experience delivering websites for different brands.
E-commerce, membership, or third-party integration experience.
Technical SEO, redirects, analytics implementation, or accessible interface development.
Experience working with designers and translating detailed layouts into maintainable sites.
TOOLS YOU’LL USE
Webflow and/or Wix Studio; HTML/CSS/JavaScript; Git where custom code requires it. Use only the platform, hosting, and integrations approved for each assignment.
Figma or equivalent design references; Asana, Slack, Dropbox, and approved collaboration tools.
THE DETAILS
Engagement + Scope: Nonexclusive freelance contract. Start with one brand and agreed deliverables, milestones, and collaboration windows. Initial term and renewals are agreed in writing. Additional work may be agreed based on delivery, capacity, and mutual fit.
Location: New York City or Los Angeles; remote work within those locations or an agreed hybrid arrangement. Collaboration and any in-person meetings are agreed for each engagement.
Works with: The designated company lead and any assigned creative collaborators. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role.
Fees: US$60–$90/hour for paid discovery, scoping, and authorized hourly support, based on experience and implementation capability. Defined builds are separately agreed fixed-fee engagements, calculated from scope and estimated hours at the agreed rate. Deliverables, milestones, payment dates, revisions, and separately approved third-party costs are set in writing before work begins; scope changes require prior agreement.
Start: As soon as mutually agreed.
Eligibility: You must be able to lawfully provide the agreed services from your work location.
Apply: Submit your résumé and two relevant live-site examples through the designated application link. Briefly explain what you personally built, the platform used, and how content updates are handled. No cover letter is required.
If this role feels like a stretch in all the right ways, we’d love to hear from you. Tell us how your skills, experience, and unique point of view can level up this team and the stories we’re bringing into the world.
Dream Three is an equal opportunity employer. We value a wide range of backgrounds, identities, and perspectives, and strongly encourage candidates from historically underrepresented communities to apply.

title: Controls Engineer
reason: Title fit +6; US +10
description_preview:
Electrical Controls Engineer
Launch Critical Automation & Control Systems
Are you an early-career engineer who enjoys working directly with hardware, automation systems, and real-world industrial operations? This is an exciting opportunity to play a hands-on role in commissioning, activating, and supporting the advanced control systems that power critical launch infrastructure.
As an Electrical Controls Engineer, you'll move beyond traditional design work and into the field where systems come to life. You'll work alongside experienced engineers, technicians, and operations teams to deploy PLC-based automation, integrate control systems, troubleshoot complex challenges, and ensure mission-critical equipment performs safely and reliably.
This role is ideal for engineers who love solving technical problems, working with cutting-edge automation technologies, and seeing the direct impact of their work on highly advanced industrial and aerospace-related operations.
What You'll Do
As part of a highly collaborative engineering team, you will:
Commission, configure, and activate PLC-based industrial automation and process control systems.
Bring new control systems online by validating functionality, communications, instrumentation, and operational performance.
Integrate PLCs, SCADA platforms, remote I/O systems, and industrial networking architectures.
Perform startup, checkout, testing, and troubleshooting activities for newly installed equipment and control systems.
Verify instrumentation, sensors, valve controls, and process equipment to ensure accurate operation.
Support operational readiness of critical launch and fluid handling infrastructure.
Conduct field investigations and system walkdowns to confirm installations align with engineering drawings and P&IDs.
Diagnose and resolve electrical, controls, instrumentation, and networking issues in the field.
Collaborate closely with technicians, operations personnel, vendors, and multidisciplinary engineering teams.
Participate in equipment acceptance testing, commissioning activities, and system performance validation.
Update electrical schematics, control drawings, and system documentation to reflect field changes and improvements.
Analyze operational data to identify reliability improvements and optimization opportunities.
Help drive continuous improvement initiatives across automation, controls, and data acquisition systems.
What Makes This Opportunity Unique
Work on advanced automation systems that support cutting-edge launch and operational infrastructure.
Gain hands-on experience with real-world industrial controls, instrumentation, and process systems.
See projects through implementation, startup, commissioning, and operation.
Collaborate with experienced engineers and industry professionals in a fast-paced, highly technical environment.
Build expertise with leading automation technologies including Siemens, Rockwell Automation, SCADA platforms, industrial networking, and advanced instrumentation.
Develop skills that are highly transferable across aerospace, energy, manufacturing, utilities, semiconductor, and industrial automation industries.
What We're Looking For
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Physics, or a related engineering discipline.
6 to 18 months of relevant experience through internships, co-ops, research, academic projects, or industry roles involving controls, automation, instrumentation, or industrial systems.
Strong understanding of electrical engineering fundamentals, including power distribution, electrical troubleshooting, circuit protection, and control systems.
Ability to interpret electrical schematics, control diagrams, and wiring drawings.
Exposure to industrial automation and PLC-based control systems.
Experience with Siemens PLCs or similar industrial automation platforms.
Familiarity with SCADA systems and PLC communications.
Understanding of industrial networking technologies such as Profinet, Modbus, or EtherNet/IP.
Working knowledge of instrumentation, remote I/O systems, sensors, automated valves, and process control concepts.
Ability and desire to work in a hands-on field engineering environment.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with Siemens and/or Allen-Bradley (Rockwell) PLC platforms.
Exposure to manufacturing, utilities, energy, semiconductor, aerospace, or industrial process environments.
Experience commissioning, troubleshooting, or integrating industrial control systems.
Familiarity with electrical design software such as EPLAN or AutoCAD Electrical.
Experience working with P&IDs and process control documentation.
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to thrive in fast-moving environments where priorities may shift quickly.
Work Environment
This position combines office-based engineering with significant hands-on field involvement. You'll spend time working directly with instrumentation, control panels, PLC systems, and operational equipment in a dynamic industrial environment.
Technology You'll Encounter Includes
Siemens and Allen-Bradley/Rockwell PLC platforms
SCADA and data acquisition systems
Profinet, Modbus, and EtherNet/IP networks
Industrial instrumentation and process controls
EPLAN and AutoCAD Electrical
If you're passionate about automation, controls, commissioning, and solving real-world engineering challenges, this role offers a unique opportunity to accelerate your career while supporting some of the most advanced industrial systems in operation today.
Job Type & Location
This is a Contract to Hire position based out of Kennedy Space Center, FL.
Pay And Benefits
The pay range for this position is $36.00 - $41.00/hr.

The Security Incident Response team works to analyze, investigate, and respond to threats before they impact Stripe’s business or users. A system that learns what a company looks like, sounds like and feels like, then produces world class creative work on its own, at a volume no human studio could match, without losing the thing that made it good in the first place.
That is what this team is building. AI plus creative, pointed at one of the last genuinely human jobs anyone thought was safe. They already do it for customers you would recognise. The next chapter is turning that into a product that anyone can pick up and use, and that is the part you are being hired for.
The founders are the interesting bit. One trained as an artist before switching to computer science. The other has been writing code for more than a decade. They argue about frame timing and system design in the same conversation. Craft is not a tax on velocity here, it is the whole point.
What you will actually build
You are one of the first engineers in. There is no platform team to hand the hard half to, and no design system waiting for you. You build the thing, end to end.
The interface.
React and Next.js. This is a creative product, so the interface is the product. Motion, latency, feel, the 4px that is wrong. A CTO who came out of art school will notice, and will say so.
The backend.
Node, the app layer, workspaces, state, the API the whole self serve product runs on.
The generation layer.
Python. Model orchestration, prompt and scene construction, assembly, and the evaluation logic that catches a bad output before a customer ever sees it.
The agents.
LLM powered agents and agent architectures. The system has to plan the work, not just render it. Multi step reasoning, tool use, branching, retries, guardrails, and the unglamorous engineering that makes an autonomous pipeline survive contact with reality.
The infrastructure.
Long running jobs, queues, media processing, storage, delivery, and cost per run. Generation is slow, expensive and fails in creative ways. Someone owns the difference between a forty second wait and a four minute one. That someone is you.
If human in the loop or preference learning is in your background, bring it up early. Teaching a system what good looks like is the core problem here, not a side quest.
"The Force will be with you. Always."
Obi-Wan Kenobi, Star Wars
Who this is for
Zero to three years as a full stack engineer, and they mean it. This is not a disguised staff role wearing a founding title. What they are buying is speed, taste and the nerve to own a surface with no map.
You will fit if:
Python and JavaScript are both genuinely yours, React and Next.js specifically
You have shipped production web applications end to end, front, back and infrastructure
You have been a founder, a founding engineer, or employee number small at a startup where your job description changed monthly
You have spent time somewhere that takes creative tools or generative AI seriously, the design led product companies and the frontier labs alike
You have built LLM powered things that real people used, not demos
You can defend a technical decision under pressure, and tell a founder they are wrong when they are wrong
You make things outside of work. Design, film, music, art, weird side projects. It does not have to be professional. It counts more than you think
Selective programs like Contrary, Neo Scholars or KP Fellows are a strong signal, not a requirement.
Who this is not for
If your entire career is a straight line through the biggest companies in tech, with no startup chapter anywhere and nothing you built yourself, this will not work. Not because that work is easy, but because this job has no scaffolding, no roadmap handed down and no one to escalate to at 11pm.
Coming from a giant is fine. Having only ever been inside one is the problem. Big tech plus a company you started, plus something you shipped alone that people actually used, is a very strong profile here.
The deal
$250,000 to $275,000 base
, set by timing and profile
Founding equity
, materially larger the earlier you land
Lunch and dinner daily
Five days a week in the San Francisco office.
In the room, with the founders, every day. If that sounds like a cost rather than the point, this is not your ship
US work authorization required.
No visa sponsorship of any kind, so US citizens and Green Card holders only
Multiple hires being made on this search
Boarding
The Empire is hiring too. Better parking, clearer ladder, nobody remembers your name.
Send your CV, your GitHub, and whatever you have made that you are quietly proud of.
Keiran Hathorn, Big Wave Digital

Description
At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.
Northrop Grumman is seeking a
Systems Engineer
with an emphasis on the
Advanced Framework for Simulation, Integration, and Modeling (AFSIM)
to join our team of qualified, diverse individuals supporting the National Air and Space Intelligence Center (NASIC) and/or National Space Intelligence Center (NSIC).
You will work on projects that focus on space, counter‑space, and intelligence missions and support modeling, simulation, and analysis (MS&A) teams in evaluating the performance of current and future military systems.
Domestic travel (up to 10%) may be required, dependent on program needs.
Responsibilities
Develop, integrate, and maintain models and simulations in the AFSIM framework to support mission‑level analysis.
Design and implement AFSIM scenarios and plugins, including object detection/identification and system‑of‑systems behaviors.
Collaborate with other modeling and simulation engineers, software developers, analysts, and government/DoD stakeholders to:
Understand mission objectives and analysis needs
Translate requirements into simulation architectures and models
Validate and document models and results
Use Python, C++, and related languages to extend AFSIM capabilities and interface with external tools, data sources, and visualization environments.
Contribute to complex technical documentation (e.g., intel‑based reports, model documentation, design descriptions) that clearly communicates assumptions, limitations, and results.
Work as part of an Agile development team, using tools such as Jira, to plan work, track progress, and deliver incremental capability.
Support continuous improvement of our modeling and simulation environment by incorporating lessons learned, new capabilities, and customer feedback.
Communicate technical information clearly to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.
This position may be filled as a level 2 or 3 based on the qualifications below.

Systems Engineer (Level 2): Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related STEM discipline and 2+ years of relevant experience; or a Master of Science degree in a related STEM discipline and 0 years of relevant experience.
Systems Engineer (Level 3): Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related STEM discipline and 5+ years of relevant experience; or a Master of Science degree in a related STEM discipline and 3+ years of relevant experience.
U.S. Citizenship with an active TS/SCI security clearance (and ability to maintain it).
Demonstrated AFSIM familiarity:
Experience as an AFSIM user or developer (developers preferred; experienced users willing to move into development are also desirable).
Experience with object‑oriented programming, such as C++ and/or Python.
Experience working on software or modeling projects in a team environment.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including ability to contribute to complex technical documents.
Ability to work both autonomously and collaboratively in a fast‑paced environment.
Preferred Qualifications
Direct AFSIM development experience (e.g., scenario development, plugin development, extending framework capabilities).
Experience with AFSIM version 2505 or later (if applicable to your program).
Experience using Jira and Agile development methodologies.
Experience with other modeling & simulation environments such as:
Ansys Systems Tool Kit (STK)
Other DoD M&S tools (e.g., NGTS, ITASE).
Additional programming experience (e.g., Python, C++, MATLAB, SQL, Java).
Prior IC or domain experience (NASIC/NSIC, TMAP models, or intel‑based modeling).
Familiarity with Model‑Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) concepts and tools.
Experience mentoring and supporting junior engineers.
